source: Written 2026-10-16 from the verified oracle text (Scryfall via carddb --verify, fetched 2026-10-16) for every card a scene shows or names, Scryfall's rulings (Dragon Tempest, Draconic Visitor, Self-Destruct, Blasphemous Act, Fiery Emancipation, Brash Taunter; Smaug the Impenetrable, Stone-Giant of High Pass, Mirkwood Bats and Big Score have none published) and this deck's notes. Cards a caption names are [[bracketed]] so clips.py checks them against the current list. Opponents' cards are placeholders, never named. The only power and toughness stated are Smaug's 8/7 (Scryfall's card data) and the tokens' (Draconic Visitor's 5/5 Dragons, Stone-Giant's 3/1 Stone Boulder, both from oracle text). Commander starting life is 40 (CR 903.7). Damage from a spell or ability isn't combat damage (CR 120.2a, 120.2b), and damage dealt to a player is life lost (CR 120.3a). Indestructible: lethal damage doesn't destroy Smaug or Brash Taunter (CR 702.12b); any other creature whose damage reaches its toughness is destroyed (CR 704.5g). A Treasure is CR 111.10a; to create a token is to put it onto the battlefield (CR 701.7a), so every token Visitor makes is a Dragon entering. Self-Destruct's X is Smaug's power, counted as it resolves (ruling). Blasphemous Act counts every creature on the battlefield, and its total cost is locked in before you pay (CR 601.2f; rulings). Fiery Emancipation and Draconic Visitor are replacement effects (CR 614.1a); Visitor's tokens are entirely replaced by 5/5 red Dragons with flying and keep none of a Treasure's abilities (ruling), so they make no mana. A token that hasn't been yours since your turn began can't attack without haste (CR 302.6, 702.10b); Dragonlord Kolaghan's and Dragon Tempest's oracle text give it. Dragon Tempest: X is counted as the ability resolves (ruling; CR 608.2h), its target is chosen as it goes on the stack (CR 603.3d, 601.2c), tokens entering together trigger it once each (CR 603.2c), and a flying Dragon triggers both its abilities (ruling). Brash Taunter deals all the damage it's dealt, even past its toughness (ruling), and Fiery Emancipation triples that too. Stone-Giant: its cost has no {T}, so it can be activated again whenever you have priority (CR 302.6, 117.1b); a Treasure's ability is a mana ability, activated while paying (CR 605.1a, 601.2g, 602.2b), and the artifact is sacrificed as part of the cost (CR 601.2h, 701.21a). A sacrificed token goes to the graveyard, so Marionette Apprentice sees it, before it ceases to exist (CR 111.7, 704.5d). Mirkwood Bats and The Sackville-Bagginses trigger once for each token (CR 603.2c). The Stone-Giant loop is optional and stops whenever you stop activating; a loop that contains an optional action is never a draw (CR 104.4b). Ganax and Visitor: neither text says 'may', so the loop is mandatory. Commander's default multiplayer game doesn't use limited range of influence (CR 903.2), so a loop of mandatory actions with no way to stop is a draw (CR 104.4b, 732.4), and no player can be forced to break it (CR 732.5). One Dragon triggers Ganax and Tempest (or the Bats) together; both are yours, so you choose their order (CR 603.3b) and the last one put on the stack resolves first (CR 405.5). A player at 0 or less life loses (CR 704.5a), and a player whose opponents have all left the game wins (CR 104.2a).

scenes.head: Smaug the Impenetrable — damage is Treasure
scenes.sub: An 8/7 flier for {5}{B}{R}, indestructible, with haste. Whenever Smaug is dealt noncombat damage, create that many Treasure tokens.
scenes.say: Smaug the Impenetrable: an eight-seven flier with indestructible and haste. Whenever Smaug is dealt noncombat damage, you create that many Treasure tokens.

scenes.head: Indestructible: aim your own damage at him
scenes.sub: Lethal damage doesn't destroy him. Aim the deck's damage at Smaug: every point becomes a Treasure.
scenes.say: Lethal damage doesn't destroy him, so aim the deck's own damage at Smaug. Every point becomes a Treasure.

cards.ph: Treasure: one mana of any color

scenes.head: Turn 8: [[Self-Destruct]] on Smaug
scenes.sub: Smaug came down on turn 7. For {1}{R}, he deals damage equal to his power to any other target, and the same to himself.
scenes.say: Turn eight: Self-Destruct, for one and a red. Smaug deals damage equal to his power to any other target, and the same to himself.

scenes.head: 8 to an opponent, 8 to Smaug: 8 Treasures
scenes.sub: The opponent drops from 40 to 32. Smaug is dealt 8 noncombat damage and stays: 8 Treasure tokens.
scenes.say: Eight damage to the opponent, who drops from forty to thirty-two. And eight to Smaug, who stays put and makes eight Treasure tokens.

scenes.head: [[Blasphemous Act]]: 13 to every creature
scenes.sub: It costs {8}{R}, minus {1} for each creature on the battlefield. Smaug and five other creatures: {2}{R}.
scenes.say: Blasphemous Act deals thirteen to each creature, and costs one less per creature on the battlefield. With Smaug and five others, it's two and a red.

scenes.head: Smaug takes 13 and stays: 13 Treasures
scenes.sub: 13 damage destroys any creature with toughness 13 or less, yours too, unless it's indestructible. Smaug is: 13 Treasures.
scenes.say: Thirteen damage destroys any creature with toughness thirteen or less, yours too, unless it's indestructible. Smaug is, so he stays, and makes thirteen Treasures.

scenes.head: [[Fiery Emancipation]] triples it
scenes.sub: Your sources deal triple damage. [[Self-Destruct]]: 24 to the opponent and 24 Treasures. [[Blasphemous Act]]: 39 to each creature, 39 Treasures.
scenes.say: Fiery Emancipation triples damage from your sources. Self-Destruct becomes twenty-four to the opponent and twenty-four Treasures; Blasphemous Act, thirty-nine to each creature and thirty-nine Treasures.

scenes.head: [[Brash Taunter]] passes it on
scenes.sub: It's indestructible too. Whenever it's dealt damage, it deals that much to target opponent. [[Blasphemous Act]] with Emancipation: 39, tripled to 117.
scenes.say: Brash Taunter is indestructible too: whenever it's dealt damage, it deals that much to target opponent. The Act with Emancipation: thirty-nine, tripled to one hundred seventeen.

scenes.head: [[Draconic Visitor]]: Treasures become Dragons
scenes.sub: If one or more artifact tokens would be created under your control, that many 5/5 red Dragon tokens with flying are created instead.
scenes.say: Draconic Visitor. If one or more artifact tokens would be created under your control, that many five-five red flying Dragons are created instead.

scenes.head: A Treasure is an artifact token
scenes.sub: So every Treasure maker here makes 5/5 fliers instead: [[Big Score]], [[Smaug the Magnificent]], [[The Misty Mountains Cold]] and Smaug himself.
scenes.say: Treasures are artifact tokens, so every Treasure maker makes five-five fliers instead: Big Score, Smaug the Magnificent, The Misty Mountains Cold, and Smaug himself.

scenes.head: Turn 6: [[Big Score]] with Visitor out
scenes.sub: Visitor came down on turn 5. Big Score costs {3}{R} and a discarded card: draw two cards and create two Treasure tokens.
scenes.say: Turn six, with Visitor out since last turn: Big Score, for three and a red and a discard. It draws two cards and creates two Treasures.

scenes.head: Two Treasures become two 5/5 Dragons
scenes.sub: You still draw two, but the Treasures are never created: two 5/5 red flying Dragons are. They can attack on your next turn.
scenes.say: You still draw two cards, but the Treasures are never created: two five-five red flying Dragons are. They can attack on your next turn.

scenes.head: Smaug's own trigger makes Dragons too
scenes.sub: With Visitor out, [[Self-Destruct]] on Smaug deals 8 to an opponent, and his 8 Treasures arrive as eight 5/5 flying Dragons.
scenes.say: Smaug's own trigger makes Dragons too. With Visitor out, Self-Destruct on Smaug deals eight to an opponent, and his eight Treasures arrive as five-five Dragons.

scenes.head: [[Dragonlord Kolaghan]]: they attack now
scenes.sub: Other creatures you control have haste, so eight 5/5 Dragon tokens can attack the turn they arrive: 40 power in the air.
scenes.say: Dragonlord Kolaghan gives your other creatures haste. So eight five-five Dragon tokens can attack the turn they arrive: forty power in the air.

scenes.head: Visitor eats your mana
scenes.sub: While it's out, Treasures arrive as Dragons, never as mana. Cast it when you want bodies or the combo, not mana.
scenes.say: Visitor eats your mana. While it's out, Treasures arrive as Dragons, not mana: cast it for bodies or the combo, not for mana.

scenes.head: Every token is a Dragon entering
scenes.sub: Add [[Dragon Tempest]], and each one deals damage as it enters. That's the next clip.
scenes.say: Every token is a Dragon entering the battlefield. Add Dragon Tempest, and each one deals damage. That's the next clip.

scenes.head: [[Dragon Tempest]]: Dragons deal damage
scenes.sub: Fliers you control gain haste as they enter. Whenever a Dragon you control enters, it deals X damage to any target: X is your Dragon count.
scenes.say: Dragon Tempest: your fliers gain haste as they enter, and each Dragon that enters deals X damage to any target, X being your Dragon count.

scenes.head: Three cards, one engine
scenes.sub: Smaug turns noncombat damage into Treasures. [[Draconic Visitor]] turns Treasures into 5/5 Dragons. [[Dragon Tempest]] turns each new Dragon into damage.
scenes.say: Smaug turns noncombat damage into Treasures. Draconic Visitor turns Treasures into five-five Dragons. And Dragon Tempest turns each new Dragon into more damage.

scenes.head: Smaug and Tempest are out: cast Visitor
scenes.sub: Visitor costs {3}{R}{R}, and it's a Dragon, so Tempest triggers. Aim it at Smaug. X is counted as it resolves: two Dragons, so 2.
scenes.say: Smaug and Tempest are out. Cast Draconic Visitor: it's a Dragon, so Tempest triggers. Aim it at Smaug: two Dragons, so X is two.

scenes.head: 2 damage to Smaug: two 5/5 Dragons
scenes.sub: Visitor deals 2 to Smaug. His 2 Treasures arrive as two 5/5 Dragons, and each one entering triggers Tempest again.
scenes.say: Visitor deals two damage to Smaug. His two Treasures arrive as two five-five Dragons, and each one entering triggers Tempest again.

scenes.head: Aim them at Smaug: your Dragons double
scenes.sub: Four Dragons: the next trigger deals 4 and makes 4 more, for 8. Then 16, 32, 64. X is counted as each resolves.
scenes.say: Aim each new trigger at Smaug, and your Dragons double. With four, the next deals four and makes four more: eight. Then sixteen, thirty-two, sixty-four.

scenes.head: Past 40, aim at the opponents
scenes.sub: Each opponent starts at 40. With 64 Dragons, each new trigger deals 64: aim one at each opponent, and all three lose.
scenes.say: Past forty, turn to the opponents. With sixty-four Dragons, each new trigger deals sixty-four: aim one at each opponent, and all three lose.

scenes.head: Every token has haste
scenes.sub: Each 5/5 token has flying, so Tempest gives it haste as it enters. Stop early, and they can still attack this turn.
scenes.say: Each token is a five-five flier, so Tempest gives it haste: stop early, and they still attack this turn.

scenes.head: Any Dragon, or noncombat damage to Smaug, starts it
scenes.sub: With all three out, [[Self-Destruct]] on Smaug makes eight Dragons at once, and each one deals X.
scenes.say: With all three out, any Dragon entering starts it, and so does noncombat damage to Smaug: Self-Destruct makes eight at once.

scenes.head: [[Stone-Giant of High Pass]]: 4 damage for {2}{R}
scenes.sub: {2}{R}, sacrifice an artifact: 4 damage to any target. When it enters or attacks, it makes a 3/1 Stone Boulder artifact token.
scenes.say: Stone-Giant of High Pass: pay two and a red and sacrifice an artifact, and it deals four damage to any target.

scenes.head: Aim it at Smaug: 4 Treasures
scenes.sub: Three lands pay {2}{R}, and the Stone Boulder is the artifact you sacrifice. 4 damage to Smaug, and he makes 4 Treasures.
scenes.say: Aim it at Smaug. Three lands pay two and a red, and you sacrifice the Stone Boulder. Four damage to Smaug: four Treasures.

scenes.head: Three pay, the fourth is sacrificed
scenes.sub: Three Treasures make the {2}{R}. The fourth is the artifact you sacrifice. Another 4 damage to Smaug: 4 new Treasures.
scenes.say: Three Treasures make the two and a red. The fourth is the artifact you sacrifice. Four more damage to Smaug: four new Treasures.

scenes.head: No tap symbol, so it loops forever
scenes.sub: Each activation spends 4 Treasures and makes 4: it never runs out, and nets nothing. Every step is optional.
scenes.say: No tap in the cost, so it loops forever. But it nets nothing: each one spends four Treasures and makes four. Stop anytime.

scenes.head: [[Mirkwood Bats]]: 8 from each opponent a loop
scenes.sub: Whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses 1 life. Each loop creates 4 tokens and sacrifices 4: five loops take 40.
scenes.say: Mirkwood Bats: whenever you create or sacrifice a token, each opponent loses one life. Each loop creates four and sacrifices four: five loops take forty from everyone.

scenes.head: No [[Mirkwood Bats|Bats]]? Two more drains
scenes.sub: [[Marionette Apprentice]]: each opponent loses 1 per artifact of yours put into a graveyard. [[The Sackville-Bagginses]]: target opponent loses 1 per token you sacrifice.
scenes.say: No Bats? Marionette Apprentice: each opponent loses one per artifact sacrificed, four a loop. The Sackville-Bagginses take one from a target opponent per token sacrificed.

scenes.head: [[Fiery Emancipation]]: 12 a shot, 8 to spare
scenes.sub: Each activation deals 12. At Smaug, that's 12 Treasures for the 4 it costs. Spend the spares on 12-damage shots at opponents.
scenes.say: With Fiery Emancipation, each activation deals twelve. At Smaug, that's twelve Treasures for the four it costs: eight spare, for twelve-damage shots at opponents.

scenes.head: Not with Visitor out
scenes.sub: [[Draconic Visitor]] turns Smaug's Treasures into Dragons, and Dragons can't pay for the next shot.
scenes.say: One warning: not with Draconic Visitor out. It turns Smaug's Treasures into Dragons, and Dragons can't pay for the next shot.

scenes.head: [[Ganax, Astral Hunter]]: a Treasure per Dragon
scenes.sub: Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, create a Treasure token.
scenes.say: Ganax, Astral Hunter: whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, you create a Treasure token.

scenes.head: Add Visitor, and it never stops
scenes.sub: Ganax's Treasure arrives as a 5/5 Dragon. That Dragon entering triggers Ganax again: another Treasure, another Dragon, forever.
scenes.say: Add Draconic Visitor, and it never stops. Ganax's Treasure arrives as a five-five Dragon, which triggers Ganax again: another Treasure, another Dragon, forever.

scenes.head: Mandatory, so with no payoff it's a draw
scenes.sub: Neither card says "may", so it runs on its own. Rule 104.4b: a loop of mandatory actions with no way to stop is a draw.
scenes.say: Neither card says may, so the loop runs on its own. Unless someone breaks it, rule one-oh-four point four B makes the game a draw: nobody wins.

scenes.head: [[Dragon Tempest]] turns it into a win
scenes.sub: Each Dragon that enters deals X damage to any target. Aim it at opponents: once all three have lost, you've won.
scenes.say: Dragon Tempest makes it a win: every Dragon that enters deals X damage. Aim them all at opponents, and the table dies first.

scenes.head: Put Tempest's trigger on top
scenes.sub: Each new Dragon triggers both Tempest and Ganax, in the order you choose. Tempest's on top resolves first: damage, then the next Dragon.
scenes.say: Order matters. Each new Dragon triggers both, in the order you choose: put Tempest's on top, so its damage lands before Ganax makes the next Dragon.

scenes.head: [[Mirkwood Bats]] wins it too
scenes.sub: Each Dragon is a token you create: each opponent loses 1 a loop. Bats' trigger over Ganax's, and 40 loops kill the table.
scenes.say: Mirkwood Bats wins too: every Dragon is a token you create, so each opponent loses one a loop. Bats over Ganax: forty loops kill them.

scenes.head: Payoff first, then the second piece
scenes.sub: Ganax entering with Visitor out starts it; so does Visitor, a Dragon, entering with Ganax out. Have Tempest or the Bats out first.
scenes.say: Payoff first. Either piece entering with the other out starts the loop, so have Tempest or the Bats out before the second one lands.

scenes.head: Smaug the Impenetrable
scenes.sub: Bracket 4 · damage into Treasure, Treasure into Dragons · the full plan is in the Plan tab.
scenes.say: Smaug the Impenetrable. Bracket four: damage into Treasure, Treasure into Dragons. The full plan is in the Plan tab.
